board.title: Get to know the board
board.text: Every column is a status, every card is a story. Click the title of a card to open the story.

move.title: Move a story
move.text: Drag any story into another column. With the keyboard: choose the card, press Space, use the arrow keys, press Space again. The step is ticked off by itself.

create.title: Create a story
create.text: Press Ctrl+N or use the “New story” button. The step is ticked off when the story exists.

order.title: Order the backlog
order.text: Open the Backlog and drag a story to another place, or move it with the keyboard like on the board.

board.move.title: Move a story
board.move.keywords: status column drag drop keyboard arrow change
board.move.body:
Drag a card into another column to change its status. With the keyboard, choose the card, press Space to pick it up, move it with the arrow keys and press Space again to drop it. Escape cancels.
The change is saved at once.

board.card.title: Read a card
board.card.keywords: card priority letter epic label tasks criteria compact one line points
board.card.body:
A card shows the key, the priority as a letter (M, S, C, W: point at it for the full word) and the points at the top, then the title.
The line below holds the epic first, then the labels as small chips; what does not fit becomes “+2” (point at it to see the rest). At its right end “☑ 2/4” counts the accepted acceptance criteria; it turns green when all are accepted.
The “Compact” button in the page head shows one line per story. Your choice is remembered.

board.columns.title: Columns and status values
board.columns.body:
Every column of the board is a status value. The columns belong to the categories To do, In progress and Done.
You can rename, add or remove status values under Settings, Status values.

story.open.title: Open and edit a story
story.open.keywords: story detail dialog title description criteria points click
story.open.body:
Click a story (anywhere on its card or row), or choose the card and press Enter, to open it. In the dialog you change title, description, points and status, and tick off the acceptance criteria.
Press Escape to close the dialog.

story.create.title: Create a story
story.create.body:
Use the “New story” button on the Board or the Backlog. Give the story a title and save it. If the title is missing, a message under the field says so.
“Add and add another” keeps epic, sprint and points for the next story.
A new story starts in the first column.

story.menu.title: Change a story from its menu
story.menu.keywords: context menu right click status sprint epic points shift f10 move
story.menu.body:
Right-click a card or row (or choose it and press the menu key or Shift+F10). The menu changes status, sprint, epic and points without opening the story.
Use the arrow keys to move through the menu, the right arrow to open a submenu, Enter to choose and Escape to close.
A notice tells you what changed, and the story is framed in green for a moment.

story.quickAdd.title: Add stories quickly
story.quickAdd.keywords: quick add plus story column sprint cell title enter
story.quickAdd.body:
Click “+ Story” at the end of a column on the Board or of a section in the Backlog, or the “+” in a cell of the Story Map. Type a title and press Enter: the story is added in that place and the field stays open for the next one. Escape closes the field.
Only the title is asked; points, epic and the rest you can add later in the story.

backlog.order.title: Order the backlog
backlog.order.body:
The backlog is ordered by priority: the story at the top is the most important. Drag a row to another place, or move it with the keyboard: Space to pick up, arrow keys to move, Space to drop.
A story you drop into another sprint section is planned in that sprint.

backlog.points.title: Change story points in the backlog
backlog.points.keywords: points estimate edit number sprint total
backlog.points.body:
Click the round points of a story (or choose them with Tab and press Enter), type a whole number from 0 to 100 and press Enter or click away to save. Escape cancels. An empty field removes the points.
If the input is not valid, the field turns red and says what is allowed; nothing is saved.
The sprint total above the stories updates at once.

backlog.sprints.title: Backlog and the sprint line
backlog.sprints.keywords: sprint planning section line upcoming running
backlog.sprints.body:
The backlog shows the sprints one below the other, followed by the stories that are not planned yet. The sprint line is the border between two sections: what is above it belongs to that sprint. Running and planned sprints are marked; completed sprints are no longer shown.
Drag stories across the line to plan them.

board.velocity.title: Velocity
board.velocity.keywords: velocity average planned completed points sprint chart table team capacity
board.velocity.body:
The Board has a “Velocity” button next to “New story”. It shows the average of your team and opens a window with the chart and the table.
The chart has one bar for each completed sprint: the frame shows the points planned when the sprint was started, the blue part inside shows the points done. A dashed line shows the average of the last three completed sprints. Hover over or tab to a sprint to see its dates, the share done and what joined during the sprint. “Older sprints” shows eight more; the table lists all sprints with the same values. Esc closes the window.
Every open sprint in the Backlog, on the Story Map and in the start dialog shows its points next to the average, for example “30 planned · Ø 21”. Use it to plan the next sprint realistically. The window has data once you complete a sprint.

sprint.lifecycle.title: Start and complete a sprint
sprint.lifecycle.keywords: sprint start complete close finish end planned running ended unfinished stories next sprint
sprint.lifecycle.body:
A sprint is planned, running or completed. Only one sprint runs at a time; the board shows it.
To start a sprint, open the board while no sprint runs: it shows the next planned sprint. Press “Start sprint”, check its stories and points and confirm. These points count as planned.
To complete the running sprint, press “Complete sprint” on the board. The summary shows what was planned at the start, what is done and what joined or left during the sprint. Choose where the unfinished stories go: the next sprint, a new sprint or the backlog. Tick “Then start …” to start the next sprint right away.
A sprint whose end date has passed stays on the board, marked “ended”, until you complete it. A completed sprint disappears from the board, the backlog and the story map.

map.basics.title: Story Map
map.basics.keywords: map activities epics sprints rows columns release planning release board feature
map.basics.body:
The Story Map has one column per epic and one row per sprint. Every cell holds the stories of that epic in that sprint.
Drag a story into another cell to change its sprint and epic.
To plan by release instead of by sprint, first switch the feature “Releases” on (Settings → Releases), then choose “Releases” as the rows (Settings → Story map).

epics.basics.title: Epics
epics.basics.body:
Epics group stories that belong together. Click an epic to rename it, change its colour or delete it.
An epic that still has stories cannot be deleted.

releases.basics.title: Releases
releases.basics.keywords: release version scope burndown history feature activate switch on enable toggle story map rows release board
releases.basics.body:
Releases only work when the feature “Releases” is switched on. Do it in this order:
1. Switch the feature on under Settings → Releases. The page Releases then appears in the navigation.
2. Open the Releases page to create a release and to see its scope, progress and history.
3. To plan by release on the story map, choose “Releases” as the rows of the story map under Settings → Story map. The Story Map then shows one row per release.
If you switch the feature off again, everything about releases is hidden, but kept.

settings.basics.title: Settings
settings.basics.keywords: fields status values features story map rows gear switch on activate definitions checklist
settings.basics.body:
Open the settings with the gear button. They have eight sections:
Fields describe your stories. Status values are the columns of the board. Story map sets the rows of the Story Map. Definitions hold the checklists Definition of Ready and Definition of Done. Releases, Team and Synchronisation each have a section of their own, where you switch the feature on or off and set it up. Data exports and imports all your data.
The gear takes you back to the page you came from.

search.basics.title: Search
search.basics.keywords: find filter ctrl+f field status epic sprint
search.basics.body:
Use the search field at the top to search stories, epics and sprints. Several words must all occur; text in double quotes is searched as a phrase.
Narrow the search with filters such as status:done: type @ to see all fields.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.body:
?  Open or close the help.
Ctrl+/  Show all keyboard shortcuts.
Ctrl+F  Search.
Ctrl+N  Create a story, an epic or a release, depending on the page.
Ctrl+Enter  Save a dialog for something new. Ctrl+Shift+Enter  Save a new story and add another.
Shift+F10 or the menu key  Open the menu of the chosen card.
Space, arrow keys, Space  Pick up, move and drop a card or row.
Escape  Cancel, or close a dialog or the help.

tour.title: First steps
tour.keywords: introduction tutorial tour onboarding walkthrough guide start
tour.body: A short, optional introduction in four steps: get to know the board, move a story, create a story and order the backlog. Steps are ticked off by themselves when you do them.

definitions.basics.title: Definition of Ready and Done
definitions.basics.keywords: definition ready done dor dod checklist criteria group not relevant gate quality check
definitions.basics.body:
Definition of Ready and Definition of Done are two checklists for all stories: what a story needs to start, and what it needs to be done.
1. Open Settings → Definitions. Add groups and items: by hand (free text) or automatic (the app checks it itself, for example “Has acceptance criteria”). Tick “may be n/a” for items a story can skip, for example “Design is available”.
2. Switch on the list with its switch (“Activate the Definition of Ready”); only then its content appears. “Insert example list” gives a start. A list that is empty or switched off checks and marks nothing.
3. In a story, the panel “Definition of Ready” / “Definition of Done” shows the items by group. Click an item: not set, done, ignored (ignored only where allowed; key N).
When a story leaves “Not started”, the app asks for the Ready list; when it moves to “Done”, for the Done list. The gate blocks the move until the open items are ticked in the dialog or set to “not relevant”; the only other way is a deliberate override (“Override the gate…”, then “Override and move”). The backlog marks stories that are not ready; the board marks done stories whose Done list is not met.

data.backup.title: Back up and export data
data.backup.keywords: backup export import save restore file json data computer copy
data.backup.body:
Open Settings → Data. "Export all data" saves everything in one file, for example getitdone-2026-10-15.json. Keep it as a backup or take it to another computer.
"Choose file …" loads such a file. Before anything changes, the app shows what is in the file next to your current data and asks. An import replaces all your current data, so export first if you want to keep it.
The file works in the Windows app and in the browser. A file that is not valid or comes from a newer version is refused, and your data stay as they are.

history.compare.title: History and comparing versions
history.compare.keywords: history changes versions compare diff version log changed before after audit sprint epic release story
history.compare.body:
Every story, epic, sprint and release keeps a history. Open the item and look at "History" below the other panels (for a release: the tab "History"). Each save is one version (V1, V2, …) with date, time and what changed. Dragging a story on the board or in the backlog counts as a change of status or sprint; changing only the order does not.
To compare two versions, click "Compare versions", or "Compare with current" on an entry, or tick two versions under "Show all changes". Left is the older, right the newer version; "⇄" swaps them. Changed fields are marked with a sign and a word, unchanged fields are folded, and the description is shown line by line.
The comparison only reads: it restores nothing. The history starts with the first change; items that existed before show "No changes yet".

team.assign.title: Team and assignment
team.assign.keywords: team person member assign assigned initials filter someone works who
team.assign.body:
Open Settings → Team and switch "Team" on. Then add the people you want to assign stories to. A name and initials are enough, there are no accounts. The initials come from the name and can be changed.
You assign a story in its dialog, in the field "Assigned to", or right when you create a new story. A round badge shows the initials on cards, in the backlog and on the story map. A dashed badge means the story is not assigned.
Above the board you filter by one person or by stories nobody works on. The search also finds stories by name or initials.
When you remove a member, their stories stay and are not assigned any more. If you switch "Team" off again, members and assignments are kept.

sync.basics.title: Synchronisation with GitHub
sync.basics.keywords: github issues import sync synchronise repository token connect feature activate switch on enable stories labels criteria write publish conflict connections roundtrip milestone epic label status icon automatic auto log notice synchronisation service switch
sync.basics.body:
Import the open issues of a GitHub repository as stories and sync changes in both directions. This only works while the feature “Synchronisation” is on and GitHub is the chosen service (only one service is active at a time). Go in this order:
1. Switch the feature on under Settings → Synchronisation (the switch at the top).
2. Below the switch, enter the repository (owner/name) and an access token and press “Test connection”. If the app should also write to GitHub, switch on “Also write to GitHub” (the token then needs “Issues: read and write”) and choose who wins in a conflict: GitHub (default), local, or you decide.
3. Open the backlog and press “Sync”. New issues become stories; what changed on one side only goes to the other. With writing on, “Sync” also publishes your changes to title, description, labels, criteria and done/open. Without the automatic sync (next paragraph), nothing goes to GitHub without this button. Stories with changes that are not on GitHub yet are marked.
You create an issue from a story of your own with “Create on GitHub” in its menu. Sprint, points and order always stay local. Without a network connection or with a wrong token the app says so and leaves your local data alone.
The sync icon (two circular arrows) is on the backlog, the board and the story map; the number on it is the changes that are not on GitHub yet. Releases are the milestones, epics are the labels “epic: Name”, and the board columns between “To do” and “Done” are the labels “status: Name”. While writing is on, the sync makes the milestones and labels it needs and deletes the ones it made itself once nothing needs them any more. Milestones and labels you made on GitHub yourself are never deleted.
The result is a short notice at the bottom, never a dialog; “Log” in it leads to the sync log under Settings → Synchronisation, which lists every run and its single changes. Switch on “Synchronise automatically” there and the app imports and compares all open issues by itself: at the start, when you come back to the app and every 15 minutes while it is open. Conflicts under the rule “I decide” are only marked then; “Review” in the notice opens the choice. After three errors in a row the automatic sync pauses until you press the sync icon.
If you switch the feature off again, everything is hidden but kept.

sync.jira.title: Synchronisation with Jira
sync.jira.keywords: jira atlassian cloud issues import sync synchronise site email project key api token connect workflow status transition board column epic sub-task filter jql criteria description write publish simulated demo
sync.jira.body:
Import the open issues of a Jira Cloud project as stories and sync changes in both directions. It works like the sync with GitHub and only while the feature “Synchronisation” is on and Jira is the chosen service (only one service is active at a time). Go in this order:
1. Switch the feature on under Settings → Synchronisation, then choose the card “Jira”.
2. Enter the Jira site (your-team.atlassian.net), the e-mail address of your Atlassian account, the project key and an API token (create it in your Atlassian account under Security › API tokens), then press “Test connection”. An extra filter (JQL, for example labels = "team-a") limits what is imported. If the app should also write to Jira, switch on “Also write to Jira” and choose who wins in a conflict.
3. Open the backlog and press “Sync”. Open issues become stories and show their Jira key (for example PROJ-12) as their ID, as a link to the issue. Epics and sub-tasks are not imported; the notice counts them. With writing on, “Sync” also publishes title, description, labels, criteria and the status.
The status is written as a transition of the workflow: a column of the board that has the name of a Jira status moves the issue there; “Done” closes it. If the workflow does not allow it (it may need a resolution), the notice says so and the change stays local and marked. The criteria are the task list under the heading “Acceptance criteria” in the description. A description with tables, images or formatting is only read; the sync never rewrites it. The sync never deletes anything in Jira.
Only the desktop app talks to the real Jira Cloud. The web preview shows a simulated Jira (marked “Demo”) with buttons to change its issues. Epics become epics (an epic that Jira lacks is made), fix versions become releases (with their dates), story points are synchronised, and on a project with a scrum board the sprint too: a sprint of Jira is made here as a planned sprint (starting and completing stay with the app). An assignee is matched by name with a member of the team; nobody is guessed, and the notice names the ones without a match. New stories come in the order of the rank in Jira.
